data.name: Bahnam
data.gender_notes: Bahnam is used as a male name in Christian naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: Derived from the Aramaic name 'Bahnan', meaning 'son of the wise'. In Christian tradition, Saint Bahnam was a third-century king of Osroene, who converted to Christianity and was later martyred. The name Bahnam carries the meaning “Son of the wise” and is chosen by families in Christian traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Biblical tradition and is also used in English, Hebrew, Greek. Parents who choose Bahnam usually hope their child will grow to embody son of the wise and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.etymology: Bahnam belongs to the Biblical linguistic tradition and is used in Christian naming. Its recorded meaning is “Son of the wise.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Bahnam total 3, giving a life-path number of 3. Number 3 is linked with Jupiter and with the qualities of creativity, expression and optimism.

in_hebrew.name: בחנם
in_hebrew.meaning: בחנם - שם פרטי נוצרי שמשמעותו עורר שמחה או הילל את שמו של אלוהים
in_hebrew.long_meaning: בחנם הוא שם פרטי שמקורו בארמית ונמצא בשימוש בקרב הנוצרים. משמעות השם בחנם היא 'עורר שמחה' או 'הילל את שמו של אלוהים'. השם נגזר משורש ארמי שפירושו 'לשמוח' או 'להלל'. השם בחנם משויך לאחד הקדושים הנוצרים שפעלו במאה ה-5 לספירה. בחנם היה איש כמורה ומנהיג דתי שחי באזור הקווקז והיה ידוע בחסידותו ובהקדשתו לדת הנוצרית. השם בחנם הוא דוגמה לשם נוצרי שמשלב מסורות ארמיות ויווניות ומשקף את הגיוון התרבותי והלשוני של העולם הנוצרי הקדום.

in_greek.name: Παχνάμ
in_greek.meaning: Παχνάμ - Χριστιανικό όνομα που σημαίνει αυτός που επαινεί τον Θεό
in_greek.long_meaning: Το όνομα Παχνάμ είναι Χριστιανικό όνομα που προέρχεται από την αρμενική γλώσσα και χρησιμοποιείται ευρέως μεταξύ των Χριστιανών. Η σημασία του ονόματος Παχνάμ είναι 'αυτός που επαινεί τον Θεό' ή 'αυτός που φέρνει χαρά'. Το όνομα Παχνάμ προέρχεται από το αρμενικό ρήμα που σημαίνει 'να επαινείς' ή 'να χαίρεσαι'. Στην παράδοση της Ανατολικής Ορθόδοξης Εκκλησίας, ο Παχνάμ θεωρείται άγιος που έζησε τον 5ο αιώνα μ.Χ. και ήταν γνωστός για την ευσεβεία και την πνευματική του καθοδήγηση. Το όνομα Παχνάμ αντανακλά τη σύνθεση των πολιτιστικών και γλωσσικών παραδόσεων της αρχαίας Χριστιανικής Ανατολής.

in_latin.name: Bahnam
in_latin.meaning: Bahnam - Christian name meaning one who brings joy or praises God
in_latin.long_meaning: The name Bahnam is a Christian name derived from Aramaic roots and used predominantly among Eastern Christians. The meaning of Bahnam is 'one who brings joy' or 'one who praises God'. The name Bahnam originates from an Aramaic verb meaning 'to rejoice' or 'to praise'. In the tradition of the Eastern Orthodox Church, Bahnam is considered a saint who lived in the 5th century AD and was renowned for his piety and spiritual guidance. The name Bahnam reflects the blending of cultural and linguistic traditions in the ancient Christian East.

in_english.name: Bahnam
in_english.meaning: Bringer of joy, praises God, or one who is joyful
in_english.long_meaning: The name Bahnam is of Aramaic origin, used in Christian traditions, particularly among Eastern Christians. It means 'bringer of joy', 'praises God', or 'one who is joyful'. Etymologically, Bahnam is derived from Aramaic roots related to joy and praise. While not directly mentioned in the Bible, the name's significance aligns with biblical themes of joy and praise. Historically, Bahnam is associated with a 5th-century saint known for his religious devotion. The name symbolizes spiritual joy, gratitude, and praise for God. In modern usage, Bahnam remains a meaningful name within Christian communities, especially in the Middle East and among Assyrian and Armenian Christians.

data.cultural_impact: Saint Bahnam is a remarkable historical figure who has left an indelible mark on Christian history. He was a king of Osroene in present-day Syria, during the third century. Despite his royal heritage, Bahnam was moved by the Christian faith and converted to it. His decision to embrace Christianity was not met with favor by his people, leading to his persecution and eventual martyrdom. Given the political climate of the time, Bahnam's conversion and alignment with Christianity were significant. While there isn't extensive documentation of his life, his story serves as an important reminder of the early Christian community's courage and resilience in the face of adversity.
data.spiritual_significance: For many Christians, the story of Saint Bahnam offers spiritual lessons and insights. Bahnam's story highlights the power of personal beliefs and convictions to shape one's life, even when faced with opposition. Additionally, it can serve as an inspiration for remaining steadfast in one's faith, no matter the challenges. More broadly, Saint Bahnam's life and martyrdom can be seen as a testament to the transformative power of the Christian faith in shaping individuals and communities over time.
data.spiritual_symbolism: Bahnam is believed to represent the biblical figure of Benaiah, a mighty warrior and faithful servant of King David. In the spiritual sense, Bahnam signifies strength, courage, and unwavering devotion to one's faith and leader.

historical_references.reference: According to Syriac tradition, Bahnam was an Assyrian monk who lived in the 5th century AD. He is venerated as a saint in the Syrian Orthodox Church. Bahnam is said to have been born in the village of Mar Qardukh in the region of Adiabene. He is known for his heroic acts of feeding the poor and converting non-Christians to Christianity. When the Persian king, Mihr-Nasar, issued a decree ordering all Christians to abandon their faith or face persecution, Bahnam refused and was taken to Persia to be put on trial. During the trial, Bahnam miraculously healed a dying soldier who was present, converting the soldier to Christianity. Impressed by this miracle, the king granted Bahnam and his companions their freedom. Bahnam returned to Adiabene and continued his work of converting non-Christians to Christianity.
historical_references.context: Assyrian monk in Adiabene who converted non-Christians through miraculous acts during Persian persecution

historical_references.reference: Another tradition holds that Bahnam was a Christian martyr in Iraq during the Islamic conquest of the 7th century AD. According to this account, Bahnam was a priest in the city of Mosul. When the Muslim army arrived, Bahnam refused to renounce his faith or to pay the jizya tax for non-Muslims. He was subsequently taken captive and taken before the caliph, Umar ibn al-Khattab. Bahnam is said to have miraculously healed the caliph's paralyzed son, converting the caliph's family to Christianity. However, when Umar discovered that Bahnam had not truly converted them, but had only healed his son to save his own life, he had Bahnam executed.
historical_references.context: Christian martyr in Iraq who was executed after refusing to pay the jizya tax and healing the caliph's son to save his own life

modern_usage.modern_context: The name 'Bahnam' is of Iranian origin and is found in Persian mythology and Iranian folklore. In Shia Islam, Bahnam is considered a martyr and is the subject of various religious stories. In modern contexts, the name Bahnam can be seen in various books, movies, and video games, reflecting its rich cultural heritage and enduring popularity. For instance, in the book 'The Seven Beauties' by Reza Abdollahi, Bahnam is a character in a collection of Persian myths and legends. In movies like 'Bahnam Guran' and 'Bahnam: The Forbidden', Bahnam is a central figure, exploring themes of love, courage, and sacrifice. In video games such as 'Bahnam's Tower' and 'Bahnam: Guardian of the Old Temple', Bahnam is a heroic character, demonstrating the name's continued relevance and appeal.
